correctness.rationale: Exact intersection-pattern decomposition yields independent Poisson-binomial counts whose total Bernoulli-to-Poisson TV error is at most m lambda_n epsilon_n. Uniform hypergeometric incidence ratios yield the limiting subset-shock means. A Poisson point process of hyperedge size masses with Bernoulli vertex marks reproduces every finite-dimensional limit. Exchangeability plus mixed moment convergence and a bounded-degree tail yield weak convergence of the empirical distribution in l1. The Poisson Laplace functional supplies the isolate moment identity, non-self-averaging criterion and Hausdorff moment uniqueness. A rounded-and-clipped rank construction realizes every finite measure. The on-disk standard-library finite verifier passed 3652 checks; it is supporting evidence and cannot by itself prove the infinite results. Exact domain and boundary conditions are stated in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: Hyperedge sizes encode group interaction scale. Even when all single-vertex degrees are asymptotically Poisson(lambda), the observed empirical degree law is random as soon as macroscopic hyperedges have nonzero intensity. The exact variance identifies a sharp, natural threshold; every possible finite size spectrum is realizable; and all its moments can be recovered from the asymptotic isolated-vertex fraction. The identification theorem is a precise structural statement, not a routine fixed-parameter computation, and addresses why the empirical histogram may be unrepresentative of a typical vertex.
